note: Closing lines, shared across deliverable kinds. This bank is authored, not measured — no line here has a performance claim attached, and agents must not present them as 'proven' or 'high-converting'. Slots are UPPERCASE so an unfilled CTA trips the placeholder check in src/lib/services/deliverables/acceptance-contracts.ts.

ctas.why: Names the action and shrinks the perceived time cost in the same breath.

ctas.text: Start with [SMALLEST UNIT]. If it doesn't [PROMISE], stop.
ctas.why: An explicit exit lowers the risk of entry.
Removes the objection the viewer was already forming.

ctas.text: Reply with one word: [WORD]. I'll send [ARTIFACT].
ctas.why: The lowest-effort commitment that still produces a reply.

ctas.text: You don't have to decide today. [SMALLER ACTION] and see.
ctas.why: Defers the decision the reader is resisting while still moving them.

ctas.text: The rest of [ARTIFACT] is at [DESTINATION]. It's the part I couldn't fit here.
ctas.why: Frames the click as completion rather than as a purchase.

ctas.text: I broke down [SUBJECT] properly in [DESTINATION] — including the part I got wrong.

ctas.why: Urgency anchored to an external event, which survives a skeptical reader.

ctas.text: I close this at [COUNT], not on a timer. [REMAINING] left.
ctas.why: Rejects the fake countdown explicitly, which is the only way a real cap stays believable.

ctas.text: If you're [DISQUALIFIER], this will waste your money. If you're [QUALIFIER], [ACTION].
ctas.why: Turning people away is the strongest signal that you are not desperate.

ctas.text: Only do this if you've already [PREREQUISITE].
ctas.why: Implies a sequence, which makes the offer feel like a step rather than a pitch.

ctas.text: This solves [NARROW PROBLEM]. It will not solve [ADJACENT PROBLEM].
ctas.why: A stated limitation makes the stated capability credible.

ctas.text: Take [ARTIFACT] whether or not you ever [ACTION].
ctas.why: Unconditional value given before anything is asked.

ctas.text: I'll do the first [UNIT OF WORK] free. If it's useful, we keep going.
ctas.why: Shifts proof of value from claim to demonstration.
Generosity as positioning; costs nothing and buys attention from cold audiences.

ctas.text: Two options: [OPTION A] or [OPTION B]. Both beat [STATUS QUO].
ctas.why: Replaces a yes/no decision with an either/or, and disqualifies inaction.

ctas.text: There's a version of this that works for [EDGE CASE]. Ask me about it.
ctas.why: Invites a self-selecting reply from the highest-intent segment.

ctas.text: Don't buy anything. Just [SINGLE STEP] and judge for yourself.
ctas.why: Explicitly disclaiming the sale is the fastest way to be heard by an ad-literate audience.
